overview: Terumo is a Japanese medical device manufacturer founded in 1921 (originally as a thermometer maker) that now designs and sells cardiovascular devices, hospital consumables and systems, and blood/cell technology products globally. The company operates through three core reportable segments -- Cardiac and Vascular, Medical Care Solutions, and Blood and Cell Technologies -- plus a newly created Terumo Organ Technologies segment established in FY2026 following the acquisition of OrganOx Limited. Roughly 80% of revenue is generated overseas (Americas, Europe, China, and Asia), with Japan the remainder; FY2026 (ended March 2026) revenue was ¥1,131.9bn, up 9.2% YoY, with operating profit of ¥176.3bn, up 11.8%.

business_model.summary: Terumo sells medical devices and consumables (catheters, guidewires, stents, blood bags, apheresis/plasma collection systems, infusion pumps, syringes) primarily to hospitals, blood centers and plasma collection companies worldwide. Much of Blood and Cell Technologies' revenue is tied to long-term supply agreements with large plasma fractionators (e.g., CSL Plasma), creating recurring, high-volume but concentrated revenue; Cardiac and Vascular and Medical Care Solutions revenue is more transactional, driven by procedure volumes and hospital capital/consumables purchasing. The October 2025 acquisition of OrganOx (organ preservation/normothermic machine perfusion devices for transplant) adds a new, high-growth, high-margin device and consumables stream serving transplant centers.
business_model.customer_type: B2B -- hospitals, healthcare systems, blood/plasma collection centers, transplant centers, and distributors globally
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas 39.2%, Europe 21.4%, Japan 19.7%, Asia and others 11.7%, China 8.1% (FY2026); overseas revenue ~80% of total

competitive_position.market_position: Global leader (with BD) in transradial access/interventional cardiovascular devices; leading share in blood component collection and plasma-collection apheresis systems; strong but more fragmented position in hospital consumables (infusion, syringes); emerging niche leader in organ preservation/machine perfusion via OrganOx following the FY2026 acquisition.

moat_factors.description: Medical devices require lengthy, costly approvals (PMDA in Japan, FDA, EU MDR), creating high barriers to new entrants and protecting incumbents' installed base.

Long-term supply contracts with blood/plasma centers and hospital system integration create switching friction, though the loss of the CSL Plasma contract (Oct 2026) shows these relationships are not permanent and large-customer concentration cuts both ways.

R&D spend of ~¥69bn (FY2023) and a broad device portfolio across cardiovascular, hospital and blood technology support incremental innovation, though Terumo is smaller than Medtronic/BD in absolute R&D scale.
Decades-old direct and distributor sales infrastructure across 160+ countries, particularly strong in Japan and increasingly in the Americas.
Century-old, trusted domestic brand with deep hospital relationships in its home market.

weaknesses: Customer concentration risk in Blood and Cell Technologies -- reliance on a small number of large plasma fractionators (CSL Plasma termination is a direct illustration)
Smaller overall scale than Medtronic, BD, and Abbott, limiting negotiating leverage and R&D firepower in some categories
Heavy exposure to yen/dollar and yen/euro translation given ~80% overseas revenue
Relatively weak presence in high-growth structural heart (TAVR) and implantable device categories dominated by Edwards and Medtronic
Japan domestic pricing pressure from biennial NHI reimbursement price revisions

growth_drivers: Expansion of the plasma innovation business (Rika plasma collection system) in North America, though partly offset by the CSL Plasma contract loss
Growth in Terumo Interventional Systems (access devices) and Terumo Neuro within Cardiac and Vascular, especially in the Americas and Europe

New Terumo Organ Technologies segment (OrganOx normothermic machine perfusion) opening an adjacent, high-growth transplant-device market with a kidney NMP device targeted for commercialization around 2030
Pharmaceutical Solutions division growth in Japan offsetting softness from discontinued Hospital Care Solutions lines
5-Year Growth Strategy ("GS26", "From Devices to Solutions") emphasizing shift from product sales to comprehensive healthcare solutions, ending in FY2027 (final year)
Capacity-focused capex (e.g., Leverkusen, Germany plant acquisition) to support production scale-up in growth areas
Secular tailwinds from aging populations, rising chronic disease prevalence, and growth in minimally invasive procedures globally

business.risk: Customer concentration in Blood and Cell Technologies
business.description: Termination of the CSL Plasma supply agreement (announced Oct 8, 2026) removes a major customer relationship, triggering ~$610m (~¥97.5bn) in impairment and transition costs and materially cutting FY2027 operating profit guidance.
Competes against larger-scale Medtronic, BD, Edwards and Abbott, and against Haemonetics in plasma/blood technology, which is now gaining CSL's business with its NexSys platform.
Rika plasma collection system reportedly fell short of a major customer's expectations, underscoring execution risk in rolling out new platforms.

financial.description: ~80% of revenue generated overseas; yen appreciation directly reduces yen-translated overseas sales and profit, while yen depreciation inflates reported growth (FY2027 guidance assumes USD/JPY 155, EUR/JPY 180).
Bonds and borrowings rose by ~¥205bn in FY2026 mainly to fund the ~¥248bn OrganOx acquisition, pushing total liabilities up ~58% YoY and equity ratio down from 74.8% to 68.5%.
FY2027 non-cash impairment of US manufacturing facilities/equipment (~¥72bn) tied to the CSL Plasma contract loss illustrates asset-impairment exposure from customer/contract changes.

regulatory.description: Biennial government revisions to National Health Insurance reimbursement prices for medical devices create recurring domestic pricing pressure.
Management has flagged US reciprocal tariff impacts (previously estimated at ~¥17bn, later revised down to ~¥10bn) with uncertainty over ability to pass costs to customers.
Evolving and increasingly stringent requirements (FDA, EU MDR, PMDA) raise compliance costs and approval timelines, especially for newly acquired OrganOx technology entering new markets.

macro.description: Management specifically cited Middle East tensions and broader geopolitical risk as factors incorporated into FY2027 guidance assumptions, alongside supply chain disruption and rising raw material prices.
Device demand is relatively defensive versus the broader economy, though hospital capital spending and elective procedure volumes can soften in downturns.
Rising raw material prices and supply chain disruption risk were explicitly flagged in FY2027 guidance commentary.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global medical device demand continues to grow on aging populations, rising chronic disease prevalence, and expanding minimally invasive and personalized medicine; management explicitly expects continued medical demand growth in the US and Europe into FY2027.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low to moderate -- device/consumables demand is largely non-discretionary and procedure-driven, though hospital capex and elective volumes have some sensitivity to economic conditions.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate -- increased debt from the OrganOx acquisition (~¥280bn in bonds/borrowings at FY2026-end, up sharply YoY) raises sensitivity to interest rates, though interest coverage remains solid (83.7x in FY2026).
key_input_costs: Resins/plastics and other raw materials for disposable devices
Semiconductors and electronic components for capital equipment

recent_developments.event: Completed acquisition of OrganOx Limited (organ preservation/normothermic machine perfusion technology) for ~¥230.6bn, creating the new Terumo Organ Technologies segment; funded substantially with new borrowings.

Reported FY2026 (year ended March 2026) results: revenue ¥1,131.9bn (+9.2% YoY), operating profit ¥176.3bn (+11.8%), net profit ¥135.9bn (+16.2%); issued initial FY2027 guidance of revenue ¥1,239.0bn and operating profit ¥224.5bn.
Reported strong Q1 FY2027 results (revenue +19.9% YoY, operating profit +60.1% YoY) and raised full-year FY2027 guidance to operating profit ¥257.5bn and net profit ¥193.1bn.

Announced mutual termination of the CSL Plasma supply agreement held by subsidiary Terumo Blood and Cell Technologies (TBCT), after CSL elected to move part of its plasma collection to Haemonetics' NexSys platform; total financial impact estimated at ~$610m (~¥97.5bn), comprising ~¥72bn in non-cash impairment of US manufacturing assets and ~¥25.5bn in transition/termination/restructuring costs. Operating profit guidance for FY2027 was cut from ¥257.5bn to ¥160.0bn (a ~9.3% YoY decline vs FY2026 actual), while adjusted operating profit guidance was maintained.
Dissolved subsidiary Kalila Medical, Inc. via absorption-type merger into Terumo Medical Corp.

guidance.as_of: October 8, 2026 revised guidance (following Q1 FY2027 results of August 7, 2026 and the May 15, 2026 initial guidance)

items.notes: Implies +9.5% YoY; unchanged through the August raise and the October CSL-related revision, which affected profit lines, not the revenue line as disclosed.

items.target: ~¥261.5bn (per August raise); reported maintained in October revision per secondary sources
items.notes: Raised from original ¥224.5bn guidance basis to ¥261.5-274.5bn range after strong Q1; management indicated adjusted operating profit guidance (which excludes acquisition-related amortization and non-recurring items) was left largely unchanged despite the CSL-related charges being treated as non-recurring/temporary items.

items.metric: Operating profit (IFRS, includes CSL-related impairment/transition costs)
items.notes: Cut from ¥257.5bn (August guidance) following the October 8, 2026 CSL Plasma contract termination; implies a ~9.3% YoY decline versus FY2026 actual operating profit of ¥176.3bn. Figure sourced from secondary Japanese media coverage of the October 8 disclosure; recommend confirming against Terumo's primary October 2026 tanshin filing once extracted.

items.metric: Net profit attributable to owners of the parent
items.target: Originally ¥165.3bn (May) / ¥193.1bn (August raise); reduced in October to reflect CSL-related charges
items.notes: October revision reduces net profit guidance materially versus the August ¥193.1bn figure to incorporate the ~¥97.5bn total CSL Plasma-related charge, net of tax effects; exact revised net profit figure not independently confirmed from a primary source at time of writing.
Up from ¥30.00 paid in FY2026; consistent with stated policy of stable dividend increases plus a 50% total return ratio target including buybacks.

items.target: Qualitative guidance only -- continued focus on capacity expansion in growth areas
items.notes: FY2026 capex was ¥101.96bn (vs ¥82.4bn in FY2025); management guidance language emphasizes continued capacity-focused investment, including productivity improvement and cost reduction initiatives at manufacturing sites.
Versus FY2026 actual average of 1 USD = ¥151, 1 EUR = ¥175; a weaker-yen assumption than actual FY2026, which is a modest tailwind to translated guidance if realized.

guidance.management_commentary: At the May 2026 results, management cited continued global medical demand growth (mainly Europe and the US), ongoing supply chain and raw material cost risk, and increased geopolitical risk (including Middle East tensions) as factors incorporated into FY2027 guidance, alongside plans to improve manufacturing productivity and invest capex in growth capacity as the final year of the GS26 5-Year Growth Strategy. Following the October 2026 CSL Plasma contract termination, management stated the decision relates specifically to the CSL Plasma agreement and does not affect Terumo BCT's commitments to other blood center, hospital and cell-therapy customers, framing the impairment and transition costs as largely non-recurring and non-cash in nature (hence the maintained adjusted operating profit outlook).

bull_case: Core Cardiac and Vascular and Blood and Cell Technologies franchises continue to post double-digit organic growth (Q1 FY2027 revenue +19.9% YoY, operating profit +60.1% YoY) even before the CSL Plasma disruption is fully assessed

OrganOx acquisition opens a new, early-stage, high-margin organ preservation market (liver transplant NMP devices used in 6,000+ procedures) with a kidney device targeted for ~2030, extending Terumo's growth runway into transplant medicine
Strong overseas momentum (Americas +12-25% YoY in recent periods) and a weaker yen assumption provide translation and demand tailwinds
Shareholder-friendly capital policy -- rising dividends (FY2027 guidance ¥36/share, up from ¥30) plus a 50% total shareholder return ratio target including buybacks
Regulatory barriers to entry and decades of hospital/blood-center relationships provide a durable moat in core categories versus new entrants
bear_case: Loss of the CSL Plasma supply agreement removes a major customer and triggers a ~$610m (~¥97.5bn) impairment/transition charge, cutting FY2027 operating profit guidance by roughly a third from the August level and raising questions about the durability of other large-customer relationships in Blood and Cell Technologies
Rika plasma-collection platform reportedly underperformed CSL's expectations, highlighting execution risk in new product rollouts within a key growth segment
Heavy overseas revenue mix (~80%) creates material yen-translation risk; a yen appreciation scenario would directly compress reported growth and margins

Elevated leverage following the debt-funded OrganOx acquisition (equity ratio fell from 74.8% to 68.5%, bonds/borrowings up sharply) reduces balance-sheet flexibility just as a major customer loss hits profitability

Smaller scale than Medtronic, BD, Edwards and Abbott limits R&D firepower and negotiating leverage in several high-growth device categories (e.g., structural heart), and Japan's biennial reimbursement price cuts create recurring domestic margin pressure
